title: Ignite 2026: Baseline security mode 2026 is GA
summary: Microsoft says Baseline security mode (BSM) 2026 is generally available with a phased rollout, adding 24 settings and extending the 2025 baseline (Office, SharePoint, Teams, Exchange, Entra) to Intune, Purview and Dynamics 365 plus a new Applications category. Examples include tenant assignment for new multi-tenant apps, blocking COM add-ins outside an allow list, no eDiscovery roles for guests, MFA for guests and external users, no Teams federation with M365 trial tenants and second-admin approval for sensitive Intune actions, each of which can be run in simulation mode first. Azure (Storage and Key Vault), Windows (VBS, Secure Boot, security processor), a dashboard, downloadable reports and regulatory mapping are in private preview. BSM 2025 is on the roadmap to become the default for new tenants.
why: This is Microsoft's own secure-by-default benchmark, and several 2026 settings touch daily operations: guest MFA, external users in the Teams lobby, blocked classic SharePoint pages and COM add-ins, and multi-admin approval in Intune. Simulation mode is the way to find the business impact before you switch anything on.
todo: Do now: as Global Administrator, open Microsoft 365 admin center → Org Settings → Security & Privacy → Baseline security mode and run the new 2026 settings in simulation mode.
Review the impact list with app owners first for COM add-ins, classic SharePoint pages, guest eDiscovery roles and apps without Exchange App RBAC permissions.
Wait: the Azure and Windows settings, the dashboard and the reports are private preview; rollout of the GA settings is phased, so the pane may not show everything in your tenant yet.
effective_note: GA with phased rollout; Azure, Windows and dashboard/reports in private preview — per Microsoft.
